title: Handshake failure playbook (on-prem egress) - draft
content:
Purpose:
Short playbook / breadcrumb trail for the TLS handshake failures we see from on-prem private deployments when traffic egresses via peered cloud VPCs. This is a personal scratchpad — steps I ran, outputs, and hypotheses. Use as a starting point for a proper runbook.

Environment snapshot:
- Cluster: onprem-cluster-2 (k8s 1.26)
- Node OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (custom kernel 5.15)
- Egress path: onprem -> customer-edge-router -> cloud-peering -> cloud-egress-nat -> internet
- Observed services: redwood-private-agent outbound to api.open-models.example:443 and to s3.us-west-2.example.com:443
- Time window: intermittent 2026-03-08 -> 2026-03-11, spikes around 03:00-05:00 UTC

How it manifests (customer symptom):
- App calls time out after ~8s occasionally. Retries succeed.
- System logs show TLS handshake errors on Agent side: "tlsv1.3 handshake failed: unexpected EOF"
- No consistent certificate mismatch. DNS resolutions succeed.

Repro (quick):
1) From a node: curl -v --resolve "api.open-models.example:443:54.23.12.101" https://api.open-models.example/health 
   - sometimes hangs at 'Connected' then: "SSL connection error: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno 104"
2) openssl s_client -connect api.open-models.example:443 -servername api.open-models.example
   - When failing, output ends with: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL
140734799325312:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:..."

Commands I ran (with notable outputs):
- sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 54.23.12.101 and port 443 -w capture.pcap
  - Observed retransmits and a few TCP RSTs coming from the peering router IP 10.200.5.1

- sudo ss -tnp state established '( dport = :443 )'
  Output example when good:
    ESTAB 0 0 10.1.8.12:50678 54.23.12.101:443 users:("redwood-agent",pid=3045,fd=29)
  When problem:
    ESTAB 0 0 10.1.8.12:50678 10.200.5.1:443 users:("redwood-agent",pid=3045,fd=29)  # NAT changed path

- sudo ip route get 8.8.8.8
  8.8.8.8 via 10.200.5.1 dev eth1 src 10.1.8.12 uid 0
  Suggests asymmetric route via peering router.

- curl --trace-ascii - --connect-timeout 6 -v https://s3.us-west-2.example.com/ 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
  Partial snippet when failing:
    * Connected to s3.us-west-2.example.com (54.23.12.101) port 443 (#0)
    * ALPN, offering h2
    * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
    * error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
    * Closing connection 0

- sudo iptables -L -n -t raw; sudo nft list ruleset | sed -n '1,120p'
  - No obvious packet mangling rules on node.

- openssl s_client -connect 54.23.12.101:443 -servername api.open-models.example -msg -state
  When failing, trace shows server Hello sent then immediate FIN from 10.200.5.1 before application data.

Packet-level notes (from pcap):
- Three-way handshake completes, client sends ClientHello, server (54.23.12.101) sends ServerHello occasionally, but in many captures there is a TCP RST from 10.200.5.1 right after ServerHello.
- Sequence numbers indicate middlebox rewriting source NAT during TTL expiry window.
- MTU fragmentation not obvious; MSS=1440 present.

DNS checks:
- dig +short api.open-models.example -> 54.23.12.101 (CNAME chain to load balancer)
- dig +trace showed no NXDOMAINs. Cache TTLs normal (60s - 300s).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Peering router (10.200.5.1) is doing TLS-aware proxying or TCP-level connection tracking that misclassifies long-lived TLS handshakes and injects RSTs when perceived timeout reached. Intermittent and more common under load windows.
2) Asymmetric routing: return path goes via another egress point and peering router sees half-conversation then resets flow. Evidence: daddr in ss output changed to 10.200.5.1 in some captures.
3) Packet mangling due to MTU/path-MTU blackhole causing TLS record fragmentation that server dislikes (less likely given MSS).
4) Misconfigured NAT session timeouts on peering box causing early session tear-down during TLS 1.3 handshake (which may last longer with larger ClientHello).

Quick mitigation tried (and results):
- Short-term: added retry/backoff in agent (deployed to staging). Reduced visible customer errors but did not remove root cause.
- Temp workaround: force TLS1.2 (-tls1_2) on some workloads — reduced failure rate (supports hypothesis of middlebox treating TLS1.3 differently).
- Coordination: opened JIRA-5821 to involve network team; they confirmed peering router firmware v2.4.1 has known issue with large ClientHello under high concurrent flow churn.

Actionable debugging next steps (ordered):
1) Get tcpdump on the peering router (10.200.5.1) at the exact epoch when failure occurs. Need network team's help.
2) Reproduce in a controlled test: run a script that opens 200 concurrent TLS1.3 handshakes to api.open-models.example from test node and capture.
   - repro script snippet I used: for i in {1..200}; do openssl s_client -connect api.open-models.example:443 -servername api.open-models.example -brief & done; wait
3) Validate asymmetric routing by traceroute from node and from cloud endpoint back to node (if cloud team can run). Compare TCP timestamps and observed source IPs.
4) Ask network to bump NAT session timeout to 120s for flows to 54.23.12.0/24 and enable debug logs for conntrack.
5) Try toggling MSS clamping on peering router to 1360 to test MTU-related hypothesis.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- If middlebox is TLS-aware it might be rewriting or terminating TLS for inspection -> certificate chain would differ; we haven't observed cert changes, so likely a TCP-level problem.
- Gathering router logs requires SLA with partner — ask infra to prioritize JIRA-5821 escalation.
- Consider client-side ClientHello size reduction (disable certain extensions) as last-resort workaround. openssl s_client -prexit -no_early_data ??? (investigate flags)
- Save pcap excerpts to GH-priv-deploy-egress-repro as artifacts.

Potential permanent fixes to discuss with networking team:
- Firmware upgrade on peering router to v2.4.3+ (if vendor patch exists)
- Route symmetry fix: ensure SNAT happens consistently at a single egress point or use source glue so return path stays the same
- Connection tracking tuning or bypass for known L7 endpoints (whitelisting)

Ticket/comms checklist for escalation:
- Attach pcap (annotated) + tcpdump time windows
- Provide ss/tcpdump/traceroute outputs and agent logs (level=debug)
- Include reproduction script and rate at which issue shows up
- Ask for peering-router config dump (conntrack timeouts, NAT pools, firmware version)

Appendix - useful commands to paste into support request:
- sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 54.23.12.101 and port 443 -w /tmp/peering-fail.pcap
- sudo ss -tnp state established '( dport = :443 )' | sed -n '1,120p'
- sudo ip route get 54.23.12.101
- openssl s_client -connect 54.23.12.101:443 -servername api.open-models.example -msg -state
- sudo conntrack -L | grep 54.23.12.101 || true

Last checks/observations (2026-03-11):
- Network team confirmed spikes align with their scheduled BGP flaps in peering maintenance window (03:00-04:30 UTC).
- Vendor reported a related bug but cannot push patch without broader maintenance window.

Next on my todo: get peering router pcap and attempt controlled repro with TLS1.3+ and TLS1.2 toggles, capture and compare.

Random TODOs (personal):
- Clean up this doc into a neat runbook once router pcap obtained.
- Add scripted pcap trimming and annotation helper.

End of draft.
